title: Tea under glass and seven days
subtitle: In which the visit is given a deadline, Hormuz a calendar, and Notre-Dame its first pope since the fire.
lede: The ceremony is over. The deadlines remain.

body:
The visit ends before the deadline begins. In Washington the two men drink tea. Over Hormuz lies a calendar of seven days. In Paris a pope enters a cathedral raised from ash.

I. Tea under glass

What was pomp yesterday is departure today. Trump and Xi close the visit with tea and the National Archives. The trade truce runs to 10 January. APEC in China, the G20 in Florida, pandas for Atlanta. Xi says the race in machines should be one of catching up, not a wrestle. He urges America and Iran back to the June framework. Trump warns Beijing not to prop up Tehran. The thrones talk about the tap without turning it. 1 2

II. Seven days

Araghchi sends, via Qatar, a seven-day plan. If the blockade, the oil sanctions and the frozen assets are addressed, Hormuz could reopen on the sixth day. The choice, he says, sits with the United States. 3

In the Red Sea the Houthis claim hits on Yanbu and Riyadh; Riyadh counts six intercepted missiles. Macron sends soldiers, radar and air defence to the terminal. Not into the war, Paris says — to the tap. 4

III. In daylight

Over Kyiv the blows fall in daylight. Seven dead, among them a fourteen-year-old boy. Zelenskyy says Trump has decided on Patriot licences — and asks him to use China's weight in Moscow. The dead of this afternoon do not wait on licences. 5 6

IV. The white guest in the ash

Leo XIV begins four days in France. At UNESCO he warns against a paradise of machines. In the evening, vespers in Notre-Dame — the first pope there since the fire of 2019. 8

V. At the edge of the page

In Sudan the army reports Sodri retaken; from El Obeid come dead. The road into Chad runs at four hundred a day. In Caracas at least twenty-nine prisoners walk free; the lists are still being checked. 9

The chronicler's close

The calendar has three new dates: 10 January, seven days for Hormuz, four days for a pope. Whether a deadline is a peace will be shown only tomorrow morning.
